goal.statement: A trustworthy read-only efficiency observation tool: every record constrained by project/window, nested records counted by a real total bound, contradictory mappings permanently isolated, an authorized Node composition main can call, a browser-safe projection aligned to the trial workspace, and usable CLI/privacy/report handoff.
goal.blockedPilot: E original 24turn/200000token/USD5 single-in-flight pilot remains BLOCKED; G did not reset, top up, refund, replace samples or research new pricing/recipes.
goal.defaultUiAdmission: Not granted. main owns root/API/App wiring; G supplies the Node composition, the browser-safe projection and the measured admission behaviour. F can run without metrics.

finalCommit: the commit that introduces this file
closedWave26Findings: a WorkEvidence could hide embedded outcomes behind a one-record maxRecords bound
workIndex A→B→A could revive a contradictory mapping depending on order
the compact projection did not declare scope/aggregation/window/coverage for F's admission

phases.result: maxRecords counts record units (outcome, container, entry, page item); containers are admitted atomically with all derived records; maxPages counts page documents while their contents still count against maxRecords; exact fit is complete

a workIndex mapping one work to two projects tombstones that work for the whole input; reordered or repeated entries cannot revive it; its entries and outcomes are excluded and its counts stay unknown

the compact projection declares scope {projectIds, aggregation}, windowLabel, coverage/coverageState and per-row unit/layer/sampleCount; cross-project aggregates are labelled; unknownCount stays null; consumerAdmission mirrors F
first runnable result: analyze → compact projection → consumer admission over the same data, plus the Node/browser entry split

composeUsageInsightsInput reads an already-authorized port (work list, evidence, history, attention), validates with the shared schemas, charges the same units and preserves every work→project pair; no HTTP server, SQL or credential
the real product surface is consumed through the existing schemas; unread works become truthful source_missing projections so they stay unknown; the probe emits a per-metric availability block
explicit loopback GET collection with streaming budgets and the verified-file replay are retained; changed bytes are refused against a pinned digest
second runnable result: the Node composition and the CLI produce identical metrics for the same two-project subject and window

two-project observation plus a single-project collection from the same instance: only the selected project is counted, no subject leaks, and the scope reports single_project; earlier windows report a known zero
finite metric groups documented for the UI (observed outcomes, interaction facts, candidate wait, partial review proxy, known usage) with meaning and non-claims; nothing else enters the view
layers and currencies stay separate rows in the projection; a partial proxy row never inherits a complete badge; unknown values stay null
third runnable result: two-project data → trusted presentation types with failure paths
CLI usability: repeated observation of the same window does not double count, reports are exclusive, and the CLI now refuses to run a stale dist over newer sources
privacy: reports never republish collection diagnostics or embedded secrets; hostile text stays escaped; 0600 exclusive output with no temporary leftovers
baseline boundaries: contradictions are refused by the envelope, a different currency/unit/aggregation is not comparable rather than converted, and comparisons stay observational
fourth runnable result: daily CLI, privacy output and interpretation boundaries

fault/bounds regression: 300-unit exact nested fit and a 299-unit short bound, nested cap interacting with the tombstone, 4500 outcomes, 200 works, 40 pages, 1000 quarantined records, 30 currencies, 16 HTTP adapter negatives
package compatibility: the declared exports include Node and ./browser; the built Node entry and the sources agree; the built browser entry loads without exposing the analysis or composition

documentation covers the input protocol, commands, count units, scope/window/current-attention, partial proxy/usage and baseline limits, nested cap, tombstone, streaming budget and the F scope adapter
this status file: five results, exact source/build/consumer/digests, measured values, coverage/losses, limits and unreached items

results.title: Full input constraints, permanent mapping and F-aligned projection
Authorized Node read composition and same-subject reproduction
CLI usability, privacy and interpretation boundaries
Fault/bounds regression, packaged consumer and final handoff

exitCodes.0: complete observation (declared sources fully enumerated, no quarantine)
exitCodes.3: partial: bounded/truncated source, quarantined records or a declared analysis bound
exitCodes.4: insufficient data: source missing or not collected
exitCodes.5: source unavailable, digest/pin mismatch, redirect refusal, streaming budget exceeded or output not writable

observation.source: real controlled product runtime (two projects) read through the real HTTP surface and through the authorized Node composition

attention.meaning: current pending snapshot after both works were accepted

nested: maxRecords 1 cannot admit a container hiding two outcomes
a container just over the bound is skipped whole
a small container after a rejected one is still admitted
an attention page is charged with its items
tombstone: reversed order gives the same analysis
a clean work coexists with a tombstoned one
the tombstoned work's outcomes are excluded
scope: entry before the window is not counted
limits: records past the bound are never validated
streaming: declared oversized length refused before reading
trickling stream times out with progress
privacy: collection diagnostics and embedded secrets never reach a report

consumer.browserGraph: no node: builtin, no analysis, no composition, no filesystem (guarded by packages/usage-insights/test/browser-entry.case.ts)
mainIntegrationNeeded: root import/export wiring for the Node composition
render of the partial flag and the scope/aggregation label in the trial UI

notReached: actual_native execution data: NOT_TESTED — the probe runs the controlled fixture driver; no vendor model or native turn was performed
operator production instance: NOT_ATTEMPTED — no operator credential was available; both the CLI and the composition support it once main authorizes
real operator baseline: none supplied; the example baseline is illustrative only
queue.waitMs / execution.durationMs: the product surface exposes no queued/dispatched pair and the controlled driver records no duration
known token/cost usage: the controlled execution records none, so usage is unknown rather than zero
main's HTTP route wiring for the composition: not delivered by G; main owns the route and the authorization
long-running stability and cross-machine performance: out of scope
limitations: All numbers are observations of recorded facts. Nothing here proves saved hours, efficiency gains, causality or quality.
review.activeMs is a partial UI-visibility proxy clipped by the real ready→accepted interval; it is never human working time.
Interaction metrics are product-record counts and carry no evidence layer.
Unknown usage and cost stay unknown; currencies are never combined and prices are not looked up.
A bundle keeps product record detail and diagnostic text and is a private 0600 input; only reports are sanitized.
Scope labels describe what the numbers cover: a two-project observation is a cross-project aggregate, not one project's total.

boundaries.userServicesPreserved: twelve 5180/8796 … 5191/8807 instances and all state/profile/tar/ledger left untouched

verification.staticChecksConfer: no runtime, native or release admission
